solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Smoother on a horse, contrary timid creatures

indicators.note: contrary asks for the little word for riding to be turned the opposite way round

parts.note: someone on a horse is up, i.e. mounted and riding
mice are the proverbially timid creatures

explanation.surface: A groom smooths a horse's coat while the stable mice scurry away in the opposite direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrary' turns UP into PU.
explanation.definitionFit: The volcanic stone is rubbed on skin to smooth away hard patches, so it is literally a smoother.

clue.text: Quietly start off country walk with swagger

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter of the country is removed

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: Someone sets off quietly on a country walk, strutting proudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' removes F from FRANCE, leaving RANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to move in a showy, strutting way, much like a swaggering walk.

clue.text: Bond seen in this part of canvas

definitions.meaning: a James Bond film of 1979 starring Roger Moore
a small sail flown above the skysail; canvas is a collective for a ship's sails

explanation.surface: A tie or joint is visible in a section of painter's canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' suggests a painting, but here it means a ship's sails.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a Bond film title and a light sail set at the very top of a mast.

clue.text: Heard bear taunt another animal

indicators.note: heard says the words are to be spoken and the result is what they sound like

parts.note: to bear is to carry, and to taunt is to boo

explanation.surface: Someone hears a bear mocking a different creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' tempts as the animal, but it is the verb meaning carry; 'another animal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American reindeer is an animal, and 'another' contrasts it with the bear in the surface.

clue.text: Holy man avoids London area collecting electronic organ

indicators.note: collecting means the shortened district gathers a letter into itself
avoids means the saint's abbreviation is left out of the district's name

parts.note: St Pancras is a district of north London, home to a major railway station
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a holy man
E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A priest steers clear of a part of London while picking up some electronic organ, a church instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: St Pancras is a London district with a big railway terminus. 'electronic organ' reads as a keyboard instrument, but it splits into the letter and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland behind the stomach producing insulin and digestive juices is one of the body's organs.

clue.text: Continuously saw jay nibbling tops

indicators.note: nibbling tops says the first letter of each of the two words is bitten off

explanation.surface: A jay is seen pecking constantly at the tops of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nibbling tops' strips S from 'saw' and J from 'jay', leaving AW and AY.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'chattering away', the adverb means without stopping, continuously.

clue.text: Headwear page needed for time in villa

indicators.note: needed for means the page letter is used in place of the time letter

parts.note: a chateau is a French country house, a villa

explanation.surface: A page boy needs a hat for his time at a country villa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed for' swaps the T in CHATEAU for P.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is French for hat, used in English for a hat, an item of headwear.

clue.text: Honour revolutionary agreement that's read on PC

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the honour's letters are reversed

parts.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
OK expresses agreement

explanation.surface: A rebel's award and a deal both feature in something read on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses OBE to EBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A digital book is a text that is read on a computer screen or reader rather than paper.

clue.text: New pair with hesitation occupying rock where some birds breed

indicators.note: occupying means these letters sit inside the word for rock

parts.note: to sway is to rock to and fro
N is the abbreviation for new, so a pair of them is NN
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A newly mated couple hesitantly nest on a rocky outcrop where seabirds breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where swans are kept and nest, such as Abbotsbury in Dorset, is where those birds breed.

clue.text: On cruiser perhaps overseas, Roger relocated

indicators.note: relocated says one letter of the word for overseas is moved to a new spot within it

parts.note: abroad means overseas, in a foreign country
R is the radio alphabet's old word for R, Roger

explanation.surface: Someone called Roger has moved abroad, perhaps sailing there on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: In ABROAD, 'relocated' shifts the R from second place to fifth, giving ABOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship, a cruiser being one example, is being aboard it.

clue.text: Bubbly, full of sex appeal. No? Yes, he is

indicators.note: full of means the sparkling wine word is filled with the other letters

parts.note: cava is a Spanish sparkling wine, informally bubbly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fizzy wine is sexy, and the answer is that the man in question certainly is.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is semi-&lit: 'Yes, he is' points back to the whole clue, so the definition is the man who is full of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian adventurer famous for his seductions is the byword for a man brimming with sex appeal.

clue.text: People replace the lid to seal good confectionery

parts.note: Turkish describes the people of Turkey, a nationality

indicators.note: to seal means the rearranged letters close around the single letter
replace means put back differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: People are told to put the lid back on to keep the good sweets fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replace' rearranges THE LID into DELIHT, which seals G inside to give DELIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gel-like sweet dusted with icing sugar, often rose-flavoured, is a classic item of confectionery.

clue.text: Section of upper storey park over east Birmingham

indicators.note: over in a down-reading or here across clue says the park word is flipped round

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a park
E is the compass abbreviation for east
Brum is the informal name for the English city of Birmingham

explanation.surface: An estate agent describes a section of an upper floor overlooking a park in east Birmingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses REC to CER. 'upper storey' is slang for the head, so a section of it is part of the brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the largest part of the brain, and the brain sits in the head, jokingly the upper storey.

clue.text: Clobber clown with it

parts.note: a jerk is a fool or clown
in means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to hit a clown, and quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing, and a sleeveless jacket is an item of it.

clue.text: See 11
Arm joint more grubby when one's fallen

parts.note: a knuckle is a finger joint

indicators.note: fallen means the letter for one has dropped out of the word for dirtier

parts.note: dustier means more grubby, dirtier
one is the Roman numeral I; one's means one has, here one has fallen

explanation.surface: An arm joint gets grubbier after a person takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one's fallen' removes I from DUSTIER, leaving DUSTER. 'Arm' is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of metal rings worn over the fingers is a weapon, and arm means weapon.

clue.text: Doctor's vehicle is touring cut-off headland — it means being late

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the vehicle's letters surround the others

parts.note: the TARDIS is the time-travelling police box of TV's Doctor Who

indicators.note: cut-off means the last letter of the headland word is chopped

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A medic's car tours a headland and he arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the TV time traveller Doctor Who, not a physician; 'it means' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tardiness is the state of being late or slow to arrive.

clue.text: The writer traverses frozen expanse, for report here in Arctic?

indicators.note: report means what is heard, so these words are sounded out

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, I; to sledge is to cross a frozen expanse on a sled

explanation.surface: The writer crosses the polar ice to report on a place in the Arctic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I sledge' said quickly sounds like the answer; the definition is a place found in the Arctic, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf of ice along a coast or cliff is a feature found in Arctic regions.

clue.text: Footwear favoured by one stumbling on vehicle

indicators.note: in an across clue one part placed on another comes after it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
pet means favoured, as in a pet project
a slipper is one who slips or stumbles

explanation.surface: Some shoes are preferred by a person who keeps tripping as they get on a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft indoor shoe for wearing at home is a type of footwear.

clue.text: Connoisseur gets enjoyment ultimately out of online drawing?

parts.note: E, as in e-mail, stands for online or electronic

indicators.note: out of says a letter is taken away from the drawing word

parts.note: a picture is a drawing

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of enjoyment

explanation.surface: An art lover takes pleasure in drawings viewed online.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of 'enjoyment' is removed from PICTURE, leaving PICURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person of refined taste in food and drink, a connoisseur.

clue.text: Cricket chiefs probing game one's played

indicators.note: probing means pushing into, so these letters go inside the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
the ICC, International Cricket Council, runs world cricket

explanation.surface: Cricket's governing body investigates a game in which someone has been fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's played' looks like a sporting phrase but defines a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small high-pitched flute is an instrument, something one plays.

clue.text: Moustache styled only partly, having a wheeze?

indicators.note: only partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man's moustache has been only half trimmed, and he is breathing noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with a congested chest and cough is wheezy, so having a wheeze fits.

clue.text: Socialist that is 29

parts.note: a socialist belongs to the political left
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A socialist is described as being unco-operative.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 29 across, BOLSHY, here as a noun for a Bolshevik or radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy, short for Bolshevik, can mean a left-wing radical, someone with socialist views.

clue.text: Mild and stout available around empty pub

indicators.note: available around signals that the stout word goes round the other letters

parts.note: fat means stout, plump

indicators.note: empty means the centre is taken out of the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A mild ale and a stout are on offer around a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mild' and 'stout' both look like beers in a pub scene; only 'stout' is wordplay, while 'Mild' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Faint means slight or weak, as in a faint smell, so it is a synonym of mild.

clue.text: Rather dim husband stops to check off his bananas

indicators.note: stops means the letter plugs the gap in the word for marking off

parts.note: to tick is to check off an item on a list

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A slow-witted husband pauses to tick off his bananas from a shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the shopping but is the anagram signal, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The suffix-built adjective means somewhat stupid, slow on the uptake.

clue.text: Russian wolfhound unwrapped pasta

indicators.note: unwrapped means the outer letters of the dog's name are stripped off

parts.note: the borzoi is the Russian wolfhound

explanation.surface: A Russian hunting dog gets into some unwrapped pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' takes off B and I from BORZOI.
explanation.definitionFit: Small rice-shaped pasta pieces are a type of pasta, used in soups and salads.

clue.text: Welshman joins Parisian who knocked back Irish cocktail

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name
qui is French for who

indicators.note: knocked back, as of a drink, says the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A Welsh drinker meets a Frenchman who downed an Irish cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses IR to RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum, lime juice and sugar drink from Cuba is a classic cocktail.

clue.text: They may be trained to fetch underwear

definitions.text: They may be trained to fetch
definitions.meaning: fighters trained to land punches, fetch meaning deliver a blow; also a dog breed trained to retrieve
loose-fitting men's shorts worn as undergarments

explanation.surface: Dogs can be taught to go and fetch someone's underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fetch' suggests a dog retrieving, but it also means to land a punch, as boxers in the ring are trained to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both fighters in the ring and loose shorts worn as men's underpants.

clue.text: Regularly reunite with drinker around storehouse

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the following word
around means the word for a drinker is turned round

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: Someone often meets up with a drinking pal around the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of 'reunite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A port or warehouse where goods are held for re-export is a kind of storehouse or trading depot.

clue.text: Unco-operative dance company, sacking old one, end in disunity

indicators.note: sacking means firing, so these letters are removed from the company name

parts.note: the Bolshoi is the famous Moscow ballet company
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: end in says to take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A difficult ballet company fires an old dancer, ending in discord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' takes O and I out of BOLSHOI, leaving BOLSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshy is British slang for stroppy and rebellious, deliberately difficult.
